title: Groupe de Galois motivique : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 9-11). Grothendieck has a reductive Q-group G (the motivic Galois group, or a quotient of it) and its tensor category C = Rep_Q(G) with fibre functor ω. A 'G-subordination' on an analytic space S is, as far as one can reconstruct, an exact Q-linear tensor functor F: Rep(G) → Hodge(S) into (variations of) Hodge structures on S. On p. 9 he describes such an F, when S is pointed, as a pair (f, α): α: Π = π1(S,s) → G(Q) is the monodromy, and f: S̃ → 𝔥 is a Π-equivariant map from the universal cover to a classifying space 𝔥 on which G(R) acts on the right.

This page gives a base-point-free version.
(1) For s ∈ S, set P_s = Isom_⊗(ω, Φ_s∘F), where Φ_s is the fibre functor 'underlying Q-vector space at s'. Compatibility of F with ω means Φ_s∘F ≅ ω. Under that assumption P_s(Q) is a right torsor under Γ = G(Q).
(2) As s varies, the P_s form a local system of torsors, i.e. a principal covering P → S with discrete structure group Γ (on the right). Its monodromy is the α of p. 9.
(3) Pull F back along P → S. The underlying local systems become canonically trivialised, i.e. identified with ω. One gets a composite C = Rep(G) → Hodge(S) → Hodge(P), recovered from P by V ↦ V ×_Γ P. This is a 'rigidified' G-subordination on P, which is classified by a morphism g: P → 𝒴. Here 𝒴 (= 𝔥 of p. 9, 𝒯 of p. 11) is the space classifying Hodge structures on ω with G-structure, i.e. a G(R)-orbit/period-type domain.
(4) g is Γ-equivariant. The category of G-subordinations on S compatible with ω is equivalent to the category of pairs (P, g), with P a principal Γ-covering of S and g: P → 𝒴 a Γ-morphism. Equivalently, it is the category of morphisms S → [𝒴/Γ], the quotient topos/stack.
(5) Level structures. Take Γ0 ⊂ G(Q), preferably commensurable with G(Z), i.e. arithmetic. A Γ0-rigidified G-subordination is a principal Γ0-covering P0 of S plus a Γ0-equivariant P0 → 𝒴, i.e. a reduction of P to Γ0 (continued p. 11). Γ0 = {e} gives rigidified structures, classified by 𝒴 itself; Γ0 = G(Q) gives plain G-subordinations.
(6) The 'topos modulaire' is 𝒴 with right Γ0-action, i.e. the quotient stack [𝒴/Γ0]. When Γ0 acts properly (discrete arithmetic subgroup), the quotient 𝒴/Γ0 is an analytic space playing the role of a moduli variety of level Γ0.

In modern terms, this is the moduli interpretation of locally symmetric / Shimura-type varieties Γ0\X as moduli of Hodge structures with Tannakian G-structure (Hodge tensors) and level structure, with a stacky quotient at the level of the full G(Q).
errors: The construction of P as a G(Q)-torsor needs Isom_⊗(ω, Φ_s F) to have rational points, since in general it is only a G-torsor over Q (H^1(Q,G) ≠ 0). Grothendieck handles this by restricting to F 'compatible with ω' (Φ_s∘F ≅ ω), as stated on p. 9, so this is a hypothesis rather than an error. It should be stressed, though: subordinations not compatible with ω correspond to other inner forms / torsors.

If Hodge(S) means variations satisfying Griffiths transversality, then G-subordinations correspond only to *horizontal* Γ-equivariant maps P → 𝒴, not arbitrary holomorphic ones. 𝒴 then does not represent the functor as a plain analytic space unless 𝒴 is Hermitian symmetric (Deligne's axioms make transversality automatic there). The page does not address this; transversality is due to Griffiths, 1968.

The full group Γ = G(Q) does not act properly on 𝒴, so 𝒴/G(Q) only makes sense as a topos/stack. Grothendieck seems aware of this, asking on p. 11 for Γ0 acting properly / discretely before taking an analytic quotient.

The equivalence (P,g) ↔ F is asserted, not proved. It amounts to descent along the discrete covering plus the representability of rigidified G-subordinations by 𝒴, which is itself only sketched on earlier pages.

ideas.what: Hodge structures (or variations) with G-structure defined as tensor functors Rep(G) → Hodge(S); their classifying space as a homogeneous G(R)-space.
ideas.modern_name: Hodge structures with Mumford–Tate / G-structure; Mumford–Tate domains; Deligne's Tannakian description of Shimura data
ideas.usually_credited_to: Mumford (1966, Mumford–Tate groups); Deligne (1971 'Travaux de Shimura', 1979 Corvallis); Green–Griffiths–Kerr for Mumford–Tate domains
ideas.where_published: Not in EGA/SGA; the Tannakian formalism appears in Saavedra Rivano's thesis (1972) following Grothendieck.

ideas.what: Torsor P_s = Isom_⊗(ω, Φ_s F) varying with s gives a principal covering of S with group G(Q), encoding the monodromy representation.
ideas.modern_name: Torsor of tensor isomorphisms / frame bundle of a local system with G-structure
ideas.where_published: Tannakian torsor formalism in Saavedra Rivano, Catégories tannakiennes (1972).

ideas.what: Equivalence: G-structured families on S ↔ (principal Γ-cover P, Γ-equivariant period map P → 𝒴), i.e. maps S → quotient topos [𝒴/Γ].
ideas.modern_name: Period map to the quotient stack [Γ\D]; moduli interpretation of locally symmetric varieties
ideas.usually_credited_to: Griffiths (period maps, 1968-70); Deligne (1971/1979) for the moduli interpretation

ideas.what: Level Γ0 ⊂ G(Q) commensurable with G(Z): Γ0-rigidifications, a 'modular topos' 𝒴 with Γ0-action, and the analytic quotient 𝒴/Γ0 as moduli variety of level Γ0; Γ0 = {e} and Γ0 = G(Q) as the two extremes.
ideas.modern_name: Arithmetic quotients Γ\D / connected Shimura varieties as moduli stacks with level structure

missed.claim: In 1965, before Mumford's Mumford–Tate paper (1966), Griffiths's period-domain papers (1968-70) and Deligne's Shimura-variety work (1971/79), Grothendieck sets up the Tannakian moduli interpretation of arithmetic quotients of period domains: Hodge structures with G-structure as tensor functors Rep(G) → Hodge, classified by a G(R)-homogeneous space, with level Γ0 commensurable to G(Z), and the quotient taken as a topos/stack.
missed.quote: la catégorie des G-subordinations F sur S compatibles avec ce foncteur fibre est équivalente à celle des couples (P, g), P un rev. principal de S de groupe Γ, g : P → 𝒴 un Γ-morphisme.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a priority/historical point: the Tannakian viewpoint on Shimura varieties is usually dated to Deligne's 1979 Corvallis paper. The page shows it already in Grothendieck's 1965 motivic Galois notes. The stacky 'topos modulaire' at full rational level G(Q) is also a viewpoint not stressed in classical treatments.

missed.claim: The modular topos at level G(Q) itself, 𝒴 modulo the non-proper action of G(Q), is introduced as the classifying object for G-subordinations but never studied.
missed.quote: Si Γ0 = G(Q), la notion de G-subordination tout court ... il y a un topos modulaire
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a non-separated quotient stack, related to the 'rational' or infinite-level Shimura constructions (G(Q)\X × G(A_f)). It may connect to the modern study of such quotient stacks, but nothing concrete is developed on the page.

deep.surprise_reason: The content (Tannakian G-structures on VHS, period maps, level structures, quotient stacks) is now standard via Griffiths and Deligne. Finding it fully formulated by Grothendieck in 1965, with topos-theoretic quotients and arithmetic Γ0, is a notable historical anticipation, but not a new mathematical result.
transcription_corrections: '$\mathcal{L}_s F$' is very likely 'Φ_s F' (Φ_s ∘ F), the fibre functor at s used on the previous page.
The insertion over 'les ... P_s' reads like 'fibres' (or 'torseurs'); '(à droite)' is written beneath it and belongs with the right action of Γ.
'G-subordination' / 'subordinations' is consistent with the handwriting ('G-subordinations') and with pp. 9 and 11.
The target of g is written as a script letter, 𝒴 here and rendered 𝒯 on p. 11 and 𝔥 on p. 9; it is plausibly the same classifying space in all three places.
